newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat wheat ends higher in thin dealings.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat wheat ends higher in thin dealings.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended higher, but traders said the move signified little because volumes were so thin.
"Volume is so light, you can't read anything into this market other than people managing positions or creating new ones," a KCBT floor trader said.
Traders said U.S. wheat markets rose early on commission house buying led by Chicago. Buy stops were hit, but the market faltered at the midsession when Dreyfus turned seller.
KCBT wheat closed 1-1/4 to 2-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with March up 2-1/4 cents at $4.08-1/4.

Traders said the market flip-flopped in assessing the possibility of cold-related damage to the new crop. KCBT July, which had been one cent lower at $3.51 at the midsession, ended up 1-1/2 cents at $3.53-1/2.
Traders said Term Commodities, a unit of Louis Dreyfus, sold 600,000 bushels of March, and Benson-Quinn sold 250,000 March late.
